findings.title: 403 docblock orphaned onto errorText, describePcsError left undocumented
findings.why_it_matters: The 403 rule that errors.ts documents now belongs to a different function than the one it describes. The block that says «403 ⇒ 「无权查看：…」而不是 `HTTP_403：需要角色 [...]`» used to sit directly above `describePcsError`; this batch inserted `errorText` between that docblock and `describePcsError`, so the block now attaches to `errorText` — which does NOT implement the rule (for a 403 envelope `errorText` returns exactly `HTTP_403：需要角色 […]`, the wording the text says must never reach a user). `describePcsError`, the function that actually performs the 无权查看 rewrite, is now the only exported helper in the file with no documentation at all. The next caller choosing between the two near-identical helpers reads `errorText`'s doc, concludes the 403 handling lives there, and ships a machine-code 403 message to users — the outcome the orphaned comment says to avoid.
findings.suggested_fix: Move the 403 docblock back onto `describePcsError` (either place the `errorText` block+function above it, or move the 403 block down to sit directly above `describePcsError`), and give each helper a one-line «何时用哪个» note: `errorText` = 后端原文 + 无信封时纯 fallback（不给日志用）; `describePcsError` = 403 ⇒ 「无权查看：…」+ 无信封时补 `HTTP_500：` 前缀。

findings.title: WORKFLOW_LABELS lookup lost its runtime fallback
findings.why_it_matters: The section-title lookup is no longer total at runtime. `WORKFLOW_LABELS[section.workflow_type].section` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'section')` when the server sends a workflow_type outside the frontend's hand-written three-value union — the expanded deliverable row crashes instead of degrading. Before this batch the same lookup was `SECTION_LABELS[section.workflow_type] ?? section.workflow_type`, so an unknown key rendered the raw enum key. The comment's safety claim («`Record<WorkflowType, …>` ⇒ 加类型不改这里 = 编译红») only holds for frontend-side edits: `WorkflowType` is a hand-written frontend copy, the contract generates `workflow_type` as bare `string` (narrowed by an unchecked assertion at the api boundary — `deliverablesApi.progress` does `.then(r => r.data)` with no runtime validation), and the backend's own `WorkflowType` enum (`pcs-backend/app/models/enums.py:582`) is a separate definition. A backend-side fourth workflow type is invisible to `tsc` and now takes the page down instead of showing a raw key.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the graceful degradation while keeping the single vocabulary: `const label = WORKFLOW_LABELS[section.workflow_type]?.section ?? section.workflow_type;` (the `??` also keeps the raw key visible, which is what StateBadge's «未知状态: X» philosophy in this repo prefers over a crash). Optionally add a runtime guard in `deliverablesApi.progress` that narrows each section's `workflow_type` against `Object.keys(WORKFLOW_LABELS)` so the api-boundary narrowing stops being an unchecked promise.
evidence: diff (DeliverableProgressPage.tsx): -  const label = SECTION_LABELS[section.workflow_type] ?? section.workflow_type;  →  +  const label = WORKFLOW_LABELS[section.workflow_type].section;

findings.title: api layer imports domain type from components layer
findings.why_it_matters: The data layer now depends on the presentation layer for a domain type: `src/api/deliverables.ts` imports `WorkflowType` from `src/components/common/workflowTabs.ts`, which is the reverse of the direction used everywhere else in this frontend (components import from `api/`, e.g. `StateBadge.tsx:47` imports `DeliverableSignStatus` from `../../api/deliverables`). `workflowTabs.ts` is a component-tree artifact — its own header says it exists only to dodge eslint's `react-refresh/only-export-components` rule — not a domain module. The consequence is that the one place the domain vocabulary lives is now coupled to a UI file: every future api module needing `WorkflowType` inherits the inversion, and moving the vocabulary later (e.g. to `src/types/`) means touching api files as well as components. The repo already has the right home for such vocabularies (`src/types/records.ts` holds `RecordSignStatus`).
findings.suggested_fix: Move `export type WorkflowType = 'SIGN' | 'CHANGE_NOTICE' | 'CUSTOMER_APPROVAL_PROXY';` into a new `src/types/workflow.ts`; have `src/components/common/workflowTabs.ts` import (and, if the existing importers need it, re-export) it from there; change `src/api/deliverables.ts:11` to `import type { WorkflowType } from '../types/workflow';`.

findings.title: Deliverable list envelope hand-copied, contract link dropped
findings.why_it_matters: The list response type was replaced by a hand-written copy of the OpenAPI shape: `type DeliverableList = { items: Deliverable[]; total: number }` where it used to be `components['schemas']['DeliverableListResponse']`. Nothing now ties the page's envelope to the contract, so the day the backend adds a field to `DeliverableListResponse` (a next-page cursor, a filter echo) `tsc` stays green and the frontend silently drops it — exactly the drift class this repo records as bug-2040 («响应体取契约类型…手写自由 dict 就是 bug-2040 的根源», src/api/projects.ts:14-16). The api module added in this same batch already demonstrates the pattern that keeps the link while narrowing the item type (`Omit<…> & { … }` at `src/api/deliverables.ts:22-25` and `:30-33`), so the page's copy is an inconsistency within the batch rather than a necessity. The same lines also reach the item type through an inline `import('../../api/deliverables').Deliverable` even though the file already has an import block for that module — the type is now sourced two different ways in one file.
findings.suggested_fix: Derive the envelope from the contract while keeping the narrowed item type: `type DeliverableList = Omit<components['schemas']['DeliverableListResponse'], 'items'> & { items: Deliverable[] };` (re-add `import type { components } from '../../types/api';`), and import the item type through the module's existing import block — add `type Deliverable` to the existing `from '../../api/deliverables'` import and delete the inline `import('../../api/deliverables').Deliverable` alias.
evidence: pcs-frontend/src/pages/deliverables/DeliverableProgressPage.tsx:56 -- type DeliverableList = { items: Deliverable[]; total: number };

findings.title: for_update flag makes load_record two read strategies
findings.why_it_matters: `load_record` now serves two different read strategies behind a boolean, and the two branches do not merely differ by a lock: `for_update=False` goes through `db.get(model, record_id)` (identity-map lookup, may hand back the cached instance) while `for_update=True` goes through a hand-rolled `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` with `populate_existing=True` (always re-reads committed state). A caller who sets `for_update=True` to serialise a concurrent write therefore also silently opts into a different freshness behaviour, and nothing in the function name or at the call site (`load_record(db, module=…, record_id=…, actor=…, for_update=True)`) says that a row lock is being taken — the lock is the whole point of those two call sites (`records_actions.py:424` submit, `:531` approval_step). The branch also re-implements what SQLAlchemy 2.0 already provides: `AsyncSession.get` in this repo's pinned 2.0.48 accepts `with_for_update` and `populate_existing`, which removes the manual `model.__mapper__.primary_key[0]` single-column-PK assumption.
findings.suggested_fix: Either collapse the two branches into the framework primitive — `record = await db.get(model, record_id, with_for_update=True if for_update else None, populate_existing=for_update)` — or split the lock into its own named function (`load_record_for_update`) so the two call sites that need serialisation read as locking operations and the non-locking call sites keep a plain, obviously-identity-cached read. Assumption: the models resolved by `resolve_record_model` all use single-column UUID primary keys, which the existing `db.get(model, record_id)` call already relies on.

findings.title: listWorkspaces silently returns a FORMAL-only subset
findings.why_it_matters: The method is named `listWorkspaces` but returns only FORMAL workspaces — a business rule (only FORMAL workspaces can host a project, enforced server-side as 422 `WORKSPACE_NOT_FORMAL`) buried inside a generically-named API method. The single current consumer, `ProjectAdminPage.tsx:52`, happens to want FORMAL only, so the trap is invisible today; the first consumer that needs PERSONAL/TEMPORARY workspaces (a workspace switcher, an audit view) silently receives a subset and renders an empty picker with no error and no way to tell the data was filtered. The method's own docstring is now also internally inconsistent: it states the backend returns 422 for a non-FORMAL choice while the same sentence says the dropdown does not offer the choice at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the filter visible in the name and keep the raw endpoint honest: rename to `listFormalWorkspaces()` (or keep `listWorkspaces()` returning everything and move the `.filter(w => w.workspace_type === 'FORMAL')` into `ProjectAdminPage`, where the project-creation form owns the rule). Assumption: the only intended consumer is the project-creation workspace dropdown, which is what the current single call site shows.
